identityReview: Ma Ying-jeou (馬英九), born 13 July 1950 in Hong Kong, legal education NTU 1972, NYU LL.M. 1976 and Harvard S.J.D. 1981. Administrative career before Taipei mayor 1998–2006 and president 2008–2016. KMT politician, former president rather than incumbent; source labels Taiwan/Republic of China are contextualized using existing site country convention. Historical party chairmanship is not assumed to share presidential term boundaries. Keep government institutions, appointed posts and elected posts distinct.
lifeStatusEvidence: United Daily’s July 10, 2026 report describes an actual July 9 meeting between Ma and Eric Chu and quotes the foundation about office attendance. This is the latest personal interaction independently located in this research pass. November foundation-investigation reporting concerns other people’s questioning and is not evidence that Ma appeared. Refresh before publication; do not infer a diagnosis from speculation or absence from events.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read selected official presidential and city career records, the CEC elected-ticket table, NCUSCR education profile, SEF signing schedule and ministry newsletter, CNA protest/meeting/judicial-outcome reports, United Daily actual-visit report and Mirror Daily investigation report. Read Commons crop/parent metadata and licence text, without visual review or current original-source permission confirmation.
corrections: Read the official presidential chronology, term header, administrative appointments and election entries. The page groups educational qualifications under the birth-year row; those degrees were not earned in 1950. Justice-minister appointment is 1993, correcting the 1996 claim in the NCUSCR event profile. Promotional descriptions of governance and success are not independent evaluation. Election dates, accession and party office remain distinct.

Read the 2012 elected-president/vice-president announcement table in the CEC compilation. ROC year 39 converts to 1950; the July 13 birthday belongs to Ma, not the adjoining running-mate entry. The 6,891,139 total is the joint ticket’s vote. January 19 announcement is not January 14 polling or inauguration. No entire 5897-line compilation review claimed.

Read the NCUSCR event profile and actual-recording description. Use the 1972 NTU, 1976 NYU LL.M. and 1981 Harvard S.J.D. chronology, cross-checked against official degree names. Its 1996 justice-minister accession conflicts with the official 1993 chronology and is rejected. Its broad first-senior-official mainland-visit claim is not copied. Do not infer an ongoing academic appointment or a current health assessment from an old interview. Video not watched.

Read the Taipei mayor roster and adjacent predecessor/successor entries. Ma’s two terms are listed 25 December 1998–24 December 2002 and 25 December 2002–24 December 2006; Hau succeeds December 25. Some historical summaries use handover day as the endpoint, but the public page follows the explicit roster’s last-service-day convention. December 25 is accession, not election day. No current mayoral office or solitary authorship of all city development is implied.

Read SEF’s fifth-talks schedule and ECFA signing section. June 28 preparatory talks and page date differ from actual June 29 signature. The authorized organizations’ heads signed, not Ma. Cooperation objectives and anticipated growth are not a measured causal economic result or proof all planned tariff measures were immediately implemented.

Read the December 2010 ministry newsletter’s substantive opening. It distinguishes June 29 signature, September 12 entry into force and the forthcoming January 2011 early-harvest timetable. Historical product lists and tariff promises are not claimed to remain unchanged in November 2026; the dossier does not audit current suspension measures or every line of the agreement.

Read the CNA Sunflower retrospective opening and dated chronology. Chamber occupation began March 18, 2014, after the March 17 review dispute and lasted to April 10. Publication/update in March 2024 is a retrospective, not a new occupation. The later services agreement is not ECFA itself. Subsequent electoral and party changes are not attributed solely to the protest or to one individual.

Read CNA’s November 7 report confirming the Singapore meeting and post-talk press conferences. It is a completed meeting account rather than the earlier departure or advance-arrival notice. Discussion and symbolic first meeting do not themselves establish settlement of sovereignty disputes or comprehensive political agreement.

Read the April 10, 2024 CNA meeting report and relevant remarks. Actual date is April 10, not April 8 predicted in an earlier report, nor April 12 update. Ma attended as a former president. Competing political claims about identity, the 1992 consensus and reunification are attributed positions, not universally accepted legal conclusions or achieved outcomes.

Read the July 8, 2026 CNA final-outcome report. Supreme Court dismissal of prosecution appeal makes Ma’s acquittal final; do not retain December 2025 provisional status or February 2026 appeal as current. Other defendants’ convictions, including Tsai Cheng-yuan’s separate counts, do not belong to Ma. This is a reported judicial acquittal, not non-prosecution; the original full judgment and dossier were not obtained.

Read United Daily’s July 10 report, distinguishing the July 8 final judicial outcome and July 9 meeting with Eric Chu from publication. The text reports an actual visit and attributes foundation claims about routine office attendance. The social-media photo was not visually inspected. July birthday wishes are not evidence of a November appearance, nor do they verify or refute private medical claims.

Read the November 12 Mirror Daily report quoting prosecutors about November 5 questioning in the separate foundation-finance matter. It includes allegations and denials; investigation is not conviction. Ma/the foundation’s complaint is not a new guilty verdict against Ma, and questioning of King Pu-tsung cannot be treated as Ma’s own attendance. No primary investigation file, final finding or health diagnosis verified.

Search indexed an earlier forecast of an April 8 meeting. Superseded by completed April 10 reporting; no forecast treated as actual attendance.
Read homepage. Its 2026 youth-program announcement is dated November 17, 2025 and is not a November 2026 personal appearance or completed future program.

Read the Ma chairman entry but found multiple Test/TestUser entries elsewhere in the rendered roster. Do not rely on the page alone for complete current staffing or unqualified organizational governance; public title focuses on established former presidency.
Opened the foundation-origin page, but it did not supply a sufficiently useful current substantive record. No founding-day or current activity claim added from it.
Read crop licence and history. One stale linked reference resolved to a source-view page and another to the original image URL; neither constituted image-pixel review. No edits were submitted.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No original diplomas, full CEC volume, original Supreme Court judgment, full investigation files, complete treaty implementation/current tariff audit, medical records, full video interviews or image pixels reviewed. Maintain allegation/denial/judgment distinctions and do not turn political claims, forecasts, ceremonial meetings or absence from events into unsupported outcomes or diagnoses.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields reviewed in seven foreign languages against Chinese and English. Preserve birthday and LL.M./S.J.D. distinction; 1993 justice appointment rather than the secondary 1996 error; elected versus administrative roles; Taipei last service day December 24, 2006 and next-day succession; separate presidential/party offices and election dates; ECFA institutional signatories/signature/entry into force/early-harvest timetable; services-agreement protest versus ECFA; 2015 serving-leader meeting versus April 10, 2024 former-president visit; July 2026 final acquittal versus non-prosecution and other defendants’ convictions; separate foundation investigation with denials; verified July 9 personal meeting versus November third-party news.
